chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Mu'addab (mercy of Allah be upon him) said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Ansari narrated to us, from Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them) saying:
Whoever believes in determinism, do not give him from the zakat, and do not accept his testimony,

Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, does not burden a soul with more than it can bear, nor carry it beyond its capacity, and every soul earns only against itself, and no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on giving zakat and accepting testimony from someone who believes in determinism (al-Jabr)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith in *al-Tawhid* to establish the theological link between the doctrine of *al-Jabr* (divine determinism) and practical legal determinism) and social credibility, arguing that if God forces actions, human responsibility collapses. The Imam grounds this disqualification in the Quranic principle that God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity (*la yukallifullahu nafsahan illa wasa’aha*), thereby affirming human agency (*Ikhtiyar*) as a prerequisite for valid worship and testimony.
